challenge.better_approach: Considered superclaude.py setting the property after the spawn: measured 2026-11-23, `systemctl --user set-property --runtime <unit> CollectMode=inactive-or-failed` refuses ('Cannot set property CollectMode'). Considered superclaude.py calling systemd-run itself: that re-implements the launch tool beside it, against RULE 1. An explicit collect= parameter was weighed against reading the env: the env is what the shell keyed on (cairn/devices/cc/superclaude at ef541167c line 623), and every caller that marks a unit for a run already passes the id there, so no caller changes.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That every service_spawn caller in a test run puts CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID in env= rather than only in os.environ; superclaude.py builds `mark` from env and passes it (superclaude.py:464). A caller that relies on os.environ alone would not be marked.
challenge.prior_art: The shell superclaude did exactly this (ef541167c:cairn/devices/cc/superclaude:623-624). grep of CairnCommons/tickets for CollectMode and service_spawn: the launch tool's ticket 60f16ffccd43 and the .py's ticket 1941e93b25a3 never mention CollectMode, so the port dropped it unrecorded.
challenge.real_collision: None: ticket d50d162c5428 and f04d5ef26a48 want exactly this outcome; outside a run the default CollectMode is kept (tooth 4 of test_a_unit_a_test_run_starts_is_the_runs), which the falsifier's second clause preserves.

answers.falsifier: With CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID in the env passed to service_spawn, a unit whose process exits non-zero is gone (LoadState not-found) within 10s; without it, the same unit stays loaded and failed. If the first stays failed, or the second is collected, this is not done.
answers.from_idea: none, because it was measured while building ticket e179281f6eff (CairnCommons/tickets/e179281f6eff-the-bash-superclaude-is-retired-its-callers-and-proofs-move-to-superclaude-py-an.json), not imagined first
answers.how: In service_spawn's systemd branch, add `-p CollectMode=inactive-or-failed` when the env handed to the unit carries CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID; a red-first proof at the launch tool spawns a failing argv with and without the test id and reads the unit's LoadState after it fails.
answers.traces_to: Law 2 (CP1-CP6 hold in the process that builds the system: a test run leaves no unit of its own, ticket d50d162c5428) and Law 3 (measured 2026-11-23: test_a_unit_a_test_run_starts_is_the_runs reds 'loop killed gone=False state=failed' once superclaude.py launches through service_spawn).
answers.what: launch.service_spawn starts a unit that a test run asked for (its env carries CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID) with CollectMode=inactive-or-failed, so a failed test unit is collected the way the shell superclaude's were.

bullets.text: The Python port of superclaude dropped the shell's CollectMode mark on test-run units; systemd refuses to set it after start, so it belongs in launch.service_spawn.

title: launch.service_spawn starts a unit that a test run asked for (its env carries CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID) with CollectMode=ina
